To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) attention to visual speech modulates activity in the auditory cortex, 2) this modulation takes place in the posterior superior temporal gyrum and planum temporate, 3) the effect is lateralized to the left hemisphere, and 4) the effect is stronger for the planum temporale than for posterior superior temporal gyrust.

(a) attention to visual speech enhances activity in the left superior temporal gyrus (STG) and planum temporales (PT), (b) attentional enhancement is not observed in the primary auditory cortex, (c) attentional enhancement in PT is not related to the degree of visual speech‐induc ed activity, (d) attentional enhancement of visual speech activity is not observed in other brain areas, (e) attentional enhancement occurs in the left hemisphere only.

(1) attention to seen articulatory gestures modulates auditory cortical responses to speech sounds; (2) the modulation is present in the absence of any heard speech; (3) the modulation occurs in secondary auditory cortex areas; (4) it is strongest in the left plana temporale; and (5) it occurs at a relatively early processing level in the hierarchy of visual speech perception.

the question how visual speech information influences the processing of heard speech.
the role of visual information in speech perception.
the neural basis of the integration of visual and auditory information in speech perception.
